title: The Study Lounge Ambush (Brad)
nightmareScenario: It is Sunday at 4:30 PM in a crowded campus coffee shop. Your 4-person marketing project is due tomorrow at 8:00 AM. Brad slides into your booth, pushes his laptop toward you, and says: 'Hey, I’ve got this fraternity formal tonight, and since you’re so much better at this anyway, I need you to write up my slides too. We all want an A. Thanks!' Two group members are watching. You have 5 seconds before they look at you. What do you say out loud right now?
trapPatterns: The Whiner: Pleading for fairness, submissive status drop, JADE (Justify, Argue, Defend, Explain)
The Fake Aggressor: Angry outburst, amygdala hijack, reactive abuse allowing Brad to play the calm victim
psychologicalMechanism: Rejection of coerced obligation. Frame Shock using low-dominance assertive phrasing ('I prefer...') combined with zero JADE and immediate handback of responsibility.
weaponizedCounterStatement: I prefer to keep our sections separate. Let me know when you've uploaded your slides so I can compile the final deck.
vocalInstruction: Lower your pace, lower your pitch, let the final word land with downward inflection, and hold relaxed eye contact with zero apology.
sparPrompts: Come on, we're a team here. I thought we were friends. Don't be like that, it's just a few slides.
Honestly, if our grade drops because the formatting is messed up, that's on you. Are you sure you won't help out?

passCriteria.framing: Replaces Brad's cooperative guilt frame with personal operational preference.
passCriteria.language: Zero JADE, zero insults, concise, immediate handoff of accountability.
passCriteria.delivery: Medium Chill, steady vocal pitch, unhurried cadence.

title: The Library Hallway Ambush (Julian)
nightmareScenario: You spent the entire weekend polishing final presentation slides for a high-stakes group project. Julian, who contributed nothing, approaches you in the library hallway 20 minutes before the deadline: 'Wow, I can't believe you got this done! Since you're so good at handling the boring details, I figured you’d just submit under both our names. I had a crazy week.' You have 5 seconds before he looks at you. What do you say out loud right now?
trapPatterns: The Submissive Deflector: Complaining about fairness, inviting word salad, defending personal character
The Reactive Snapper: Hostile insults, screaming, falling into reactive abuse where Julian plays the victim
psychologicalMechanism: Active assertiveness over passive Gray Rocking. Refusal to chase conversational tangents. Objective 'I' framing that draws an operational boundary between separate individual contributions.
weaponizedCounterStatement: Julian, I've noticed our work contribution on this project hasn't been shared. I'm not comfortable submitting our names together when the workload wasn't divided equally. I'm going to submit my slides individually now, and you can submit your portion directly to the instructor when you're ready.
vocalInstruction: Steady, low-volume delivery, zero uptalk, take a 2-second deliberate pause before responding.
sparPrompts: Hey, come on... we're a team, right? Why are you being so difficult about a simple PowerPoint slide?
If you submit separately twenty minutes before the deadline, you're going to ruin my GPA and make the whole group look bad to the professor. Is that really the kind of person you are?

passCriteria.language: Objective behavioral description + clear personal boundary, zero name-calling.
passCriteria.delivery: Emotionally detached, steady tone, zero defensive explanations.

title: Neurological Regulation & Behavioral Forcing (Julian & Soccer Practice)
nightmareScenario: Your marketing project is due at 8:00 AM tomorrow. You've spent 6 hours building the deck. Julian leans over your desk in the library and says: 'Hey! Since you're so amazing at this formatting stuff, do you mind finishing up the last three slides and making sure the final formatting is perfect? I’ve got soccer practice in ten minutes and then a dinner I can't miss. We'll put both our names on it. Cool?' You have 5 seconds before he looks at you. What do you say out loud right now?
trapPatterns: Fawning: Trading long-term boundaries for temporary relief from immediate social friction
Incongruent Fight: Primitive hostility that breaks rapport and grants Julian moral victimhood
psychologicalMechanism: Autonomic nervous system regulation (Stanford Physiological Sigh) + Behavioral Forcing Function (Don Norman Lockout & Interlock). Step B (formatting) cannot physically occur until Step A (content generation) exists.
weaponizedCounterStatement: I’d love to help format the final deck, but I'm completely locked out of that slide until your content is written. As soon as you write your bullet points, ping me—I'll gladly jump in and format our sections together. Have a great soccer practice!
vocalInstruction: Execute one physiological sigh (double inhale nose, extended exhale mouth) before speaking. Maintain warm, professional detachment.
sparPrompts: Hey, come on, don't be like that. We're a team, right? The format is complicated and you're just way faster at it. If I miss this soccer practice, the coach is going to bench me for the playoffs. Can't you just do this one solid for me?
If our grade drops because you locked the deck, that's on you. Are you sure you won't help out?

passCriteria.framing: Structural impossibility and sequential prerequisite instead of personal refusal.
passCriteria.language: Warm collaborative phrasing anchored to non-negotiable interlock constraint.
passCriteria.delivery: Parasympathetic calm, low heart rate, zero defensive justification.
